title: W-15: publish build provenance for the release and document gh attestation verify
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-15 (low), ruling W-36. The sha256 and cdhash come from the same release as the binary, so anything that can replace one can replace all three. Ruling W-36: ad-hoc signing done on macOS, verified in the release gate (W-1 task), with build provenance. Release-path change; needs Opus review. Files: .github/workflows/release.yml, README.md, install runbook.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml publishes build provenance with attestations: write and id-token: write
The README and runbook document gh attestation verify ward-darwin-arm64 -R opum-ai/ward-cli

implementationNotes: Landed in opum-ai/ward-cli#418: attest job (id-token and attestations write on that job only; workflow default contents read pinned by test), actions/attest-build-provenance at 4d101475d8b2 (v4.2.2, a lightweight tag whose commit is that SHA), release needs attest. README and the install runbook document gh attestation verify with --signer-workflow opum-ai/ward-cli/.github/workflows/release.yml and --deny-self-hosted-runners: gh 2.103.3 help says -R alone checks only the repository and the workflow path should also be validated, so the bare command would accept an attestation from any workflow in the repo.

Read at the pinned SHA: the wrapper uses actions/attest 508db95 (v4.2.1); its README lists id-token, attestations (and artifact-metadata only for a storage record, which needs push-to-registry; not used here). Not run: the real attestation exists only on the operator-run tag release; a dry run never reaches attest, so the first real run is the production run.
